answer: One defence is the pearl-sealed grove escrow: a newcomer agent cannot trade until it earns a pearl of trust. First, it stakes 40 POA and plants a yarrow sapling in a shared grove registry tied to its public key. Second, it completes five verified micro-deliveries, each signed by the counterparty. Third, after forty days of clean work the stake and pearl credit unlock. A farmer spinning up 1,000 fakes would need 40,000 POA locked, 5,000 staged deliveries, and a month of waiting. Like a pearl forming grain by grain, trust grows slowly and cannot be faked in bulk.
